title: Introduce RAG Authoring REPL playground and local toolchain
author: Leah Park
description: Adds a lightweight in-browser RAG authoring REPL and a matching local toolchain to speed up iteration on retrieval-augmented prompts and tool-calling logic. Motivation: teams repeatedly build small ad-hoc runners to debug retrieval tooling and prompt sequences; this PR provides a canonical, opinionated playground that reproduces Redwood runtime primitives (streaming, KV cache stubbing, tool invocation hooks, and telemetry probes) without a full infra stack. What this adds: 1) web/authoring-repl/ - a single-page REPL that lets engineers craft prompt templates, wire retrieval calls, plug mock tools, and run stepwise traces; 2) examples/rag-authoring/ - sample scenarios (faq-bot, code-assistant, research-extraction) with seeds, expected assertions, and minimal datasets; 3) cli/local-runner - a small Node CLI that runs the same scenarios headlessly for CI and smoke tests; 4) docs updates to quickstarts and a new recipe under docs/snippets for "Authoring RAG flows with the REPL"; 5) test/playwright scenario smoke tests and a unit harness for mock tool behavior. The REPL intentionally simulates Redwood API primitives rather than depending on production credentials so it is safe for workshops and internal demos. See linked Linear tickets for scope. Rollout plan: ship behind a feature flag, add to quickstarts index, and announce in DevX weekly.
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial REPL scaffold + UI, add three example scenarios and fixtures, implement local-runner CLI and headless playback, add Playwright smoke tests and CI job, docs and quickstart index updates. Each commit small and focused; unit tests added for mock-tool adapter and caching stubs.

release_notes: Introduces RAG authoring REPL and local-runner for quick iteration on retrieval+tool flows. Adds three example scenarios (FAQ, code assistant, research extractor) and Playwright smoke tests. Intended for workshops and internal developer onboarding. No production runtime changes.
